core.title: No ad-hoc print logging in application source
core.given: An application source file of the stack (not a test, vendored or build file).
core.when: Code calls the stack's ad-hoc print or logging construct, for any purpose (log, diagnostic or CLI interface output).
core.then: Do not use the stack's ad-hoc print or logging calls in application source; log via the structured logger.
prefer: Emit log output through the structured logger; the logger owns level, timestamp and correlation.

A CLI entry point whose standard output IS its user interface writes that output through the raw stream-write construct (errors to the error stream); it says plainly that it is the interface, not a log.
avoid: Ad-hoc print calls for log output, including the error-stream variant: the error stream is still unlevelled, uncorrelated and not queryable.
Per-file exemptions from this rule (none exist), and raw stream writes for output that is really a log rather than a CLI's interface.
unless: Occurrences inside a comment or string literal (masked by the scan, never flagged).
Test files and vendored or build directories.
core.why: The ad-hoc print call carries no level, timestamp or request correlation, so production logs become one unfilterable stream; and a module shared across server and client runtimes may send its output to the end user instead of the operator.
evidence: The stack's hygiene check reports no unlevelled-print finding across in-scope application source (not only changed files).
Review: log output goes through the structured logger (levels, timestamps, correlation); CLI interface output uses the raw stream-write construct.
verification: A source-hygiene validator flags every call to the stack's ad-hoc print constructs in application source, scanning with strings and comments masked, so an occurrence inside a comment or string literal never trips the rule.
The scan covers all in-scope application source, not only changed files.

Test files and vendored or build directories are excluded from the scan; the exclusion only scopes the check, it does not weaken the obligation on application source. The exact classification of test, vendored and build files is owned by this rule's checker, not by the stack-wide never-scanned tree list.
Only the ad-hoc print constructs are matched; the CLI's raw stream writes to the standard streams are not flagged, and no per-file exemption from this rule exists.

fires: A boundary handler or application-layer service module in application source logs with the ad-hoc print call.
A module shared by the server and client runtimes uses the ad-hoc print call in an error path.
A CLI entry point in application source prints its user-facing output with the ad-hoc print call.
An existing application source file already contains an ad-hoc print call.
doesNotFire: The ad-hoc print construct appears only inside a comment or a string literal.
Ad-hoc print calls in test files.
Ad-hoc print calls in vendored or build output directories.
A CLI writes its user-facing output through the raw stream-write construct.

neutralityNotes: The concrete forbidden call set (console.*), the structured logger and the CLI stream-write construct have no existing vocabulary key; they are carried as data through three proposed idiom keys (idiom.adhoc_print_calls, idiom.structured_logger, idiom.cli_interface_output), so the core names only the neutral concepts 'ad-hoc print call', 'structured logger' and 'raw stream write'. Detector, validator and finding ids (bun_security_hygiene_detector, LOGGING-PRINT-001) stay Bun-only per the notProfileKeys list. The exclusion of test files and vendored or build directories is stated in the core exactly as Bun states it and stays in this rule's verification: bun.json defers the exact classification to its checker (it lists no concrete excluded paths for this rule), so the exclusion is not mapped to the stack-wide never-scanned list roots.excluded, and no broader 'generated source' exemption is introduced. activation.facts[0] (language) has no slot in the closed fact vocabulary, so language scoping moved to profile key tooling.languages. The 'browser devtools' consequence is generalized to client runtimes, which preserves the obligation without naming a runtime.
